Details: The failing test `X5455_ExtendedTimestampTest.testGettersSetters()` in the `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip` package is encountering issues under JDK 9. It seems that the failure is related to a potentially incorrect value being returned from `getTime()`. This could be due to changes introduced in JDK 9, possibly linked to the details mentioned in the issue <https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8073497>. The test tries to set a modification time that exceeds 32 bits and expects an `IllegalArgumentException` to be thrown, indicating that the time is too large. However, this exception is not being thrown as expected, leading to the test failure.

The issue may be connected to JDK 9 changes affecting the behavior of `getTime()` or the handling of modification times in the test environment. It is recommended to review the impact of the JDK 9 changes and ensure that the test logic aligns with the updated behavior to address the test failure.

Additionally, considering the switch to JDK 9, it might be useful to confirm if there are any specific requirements or adjustments needed in the code related to the handling of timestamps or time-related operations.

I will now suggest potential methods to be fixed based on this diagnosis.
